rows.note: Use this for the ordinary sausage-shaped food rather than a patty.

example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 hoeng1 coeng2 hou2 hoeng1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a connection or relationship between people, things, events, or ideas.

example.english: These two things have a link.
example.jyutping: ni1 loeng5 gin6 si6 jau5 gwaan1 hai6 gaa3

rows.note: Use this colloquial phrase when “link” means arrange to meet up with someone.

example.english: We’ll link up for dim sum on Saturday.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 joek3 maai4 sing1 kei4 luk6 jam2 caa4

rows.note: Use this as the everyday choice for physically connecting or joining things together.

example.english: Link the two wires together and it’ll be fine.
example.traditional: 將兩條電線連埋一齊就得喇。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 loeng5 tiu4 din6 sin3 lin4 maai4 jat1 cai4 zau6 dak1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a website or page containing a link that leads to another page.

example.english: This webpage has a link to another page.
example.traditional: 呢個網頁有條連到另一頁嘅連結。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 mong5 jip6 jau5 tiu4 lin4 dou3 ling6 jat1 jip6 ge3 lin4 git3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a connecting service or connection between transport routes or systems.

example.english: This bus provides a link to the MTR.
example.traditional: 呢班巴士可以接駁地鐵。
example.jyutping: ni1 baan1 baa1 si2 ho2 ji5 zip3 bok3 dei6 tit3

rows.jyutping: cyun4 tiu4 lin4 git3 bei2 jan4
rows.note: Use this when supplying somebody with a hyperlink, usually in a message or chat.

example.english: I’m sending someone a link now and waiting for them to reply.
example.traditional: 我而家傳條連結畀人，等佢覆我。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 cyun4 tiu4 lin4 git3 bei2 jan4 dang2 keoi5 fuk1 ngo5

rows.note: Use this for one physical ring or element of a chain.

example.english: A link has come off the chain.
example.jyutping: tiu4 lin4 lat1 zo2 jat1 go3 lin4 waan4
